artworks.title: Fish Hawk

artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper

artworks.title: Whip-poor-will
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a natural scene with birds, insects, and foliage. Two whip-poor-wills are perched on a branch with a background of green leaves. One bird is flying, showing its brown and white feathers extended. There are two moths with brown and pink wings, and red and yellow patterns, as well as a caterpillar on a leaf. The details are meticulously rendered, capturing the textures of feathers, leaves, and bark with fine lines and shading. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed and accurate illustrations of birds in their habitats.

artworks.title: House Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: There are two small birds interacting around a piece of worn fabric on a branch, serving as a nesting site with several birds peeking out from it. The color palette includes shades of brown and tan for the birds, with the branch and fabric in hues of brown and gray. The exposed wood of the branch has hints of blue and green from moss. The central fabric is on the right with one bird perched on it, and another bird partially upside down near the entrance to the nest, located in the center to the left. The upper bird is above the opening, while the lower bird holds a small insect in its beak, facing the nest entrance.

artworks.title: Blue-grey Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two blue birds perched on different branches of a leafy plant. The birds are depicted with blue plumage and detailed markings, set in a natural environment with green leaves and green seeds. The branches provide a lattice structure to the composition.

artworks.title: Yellow-throated Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a Yellow-throated Warbler perched on a branch with green leaves and seed pods. The bird has a yellow throat, blue-gray back, and black and white wing patterns. It is positioned towards the bottom right of the image amidst the leaves and seed pods on the branch.

artworks.title: Black Warrior
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two hawks are depicted in a painting. The birds are detailed and realistic, showcasing their feather patterns and talons. One hawk is standing upright facing the viewer with its head turned to the side, displaying its plumage which ranges from dark browns to lighter shades blending into the wings. The second hawk is in a dynamic pose with wings partially spread and head bent downwards. Branches with a rough texture are shown in the background. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Florida Jays
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two blue birds perched on a tree branch with orange to yellow fruits. The birds have vibrant blue plumage and the tree is filled with green leaves and colorful fruits. One bird is pecking at a fruit while the other has its wings spread out.

artworks.title: Autumnal Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two colorful birds perched on a branch with green leaves. The birds have vibrant feathers and are surrounded by detailed green foliage and unripe pine cones on the branch. The birds' plumage displays shades of olive green, cream, brown, and yellow. The leaves are detailed, showing veins and color variations of green. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed depictions of birds and nature.

artworks.title: Nashville Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on branches with red berries and green leaves.

artworks.title: Black and White Creeper
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird perched on a branch with pine cones. The bird has black and white patterns on its feathers and is on a coniferous tree branch with green pine needles and brown pine cones at different stages of development. The bird is positioned diagonally, giving a sense of movement. The illustration style is detailed and accurate, reminiscent of John James Audubon's work.

artworks.title: Broad-winged Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds of prey perched on a branch with green foliage. It features two hawks—one larger with brown and white plumage standing upright on a branch, and another with fanned tail and partially outstretched wings below. Both birds are detailed anatomically, showcasing their feathers and patterns. They are surrounded by green leaves with variations in shade, suggesting light and shadow. The scene is set against a neutral background, emphasizing the birds and foliage. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's realistic bird paintings.

artworks.title: Pigeon Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a branch with leaves. The birds are detailed and realistic, one positioned towards the top of the branch and the other below it. The branch curves gently and is complemented by large green leaves with some brownish tones. The background is a pale, neutral tone.

artworks.title: Sea-side Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched among wild rose branches. The birds have brown, gray, and black plumage and are positioned at different heights. The rose branches have green leaves and pink blooming roses with yellow centers. The color palette includes green, pink, brown, and gray, creating a visually appealing composition.

artworks.title: Bay-winged Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a bird on a piece of wood in front of a blooming cactus plant. The color palette includes greens, browns, grays, and yellows. The bird is facing slightly to the left, with its tail and wings extending to the right. The cactus has branches and yellow flowers blooming on it against a plain background.

artworks.title: Blue-eyed Yellow Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a yellow bird perched on a branch with trailing blue and purple flowers. The artwork depicts a bright yellow bird sitting amid lush green leaves. The bird is delicately clutching a slender branch that is draped with clusters of pastel-colored flowers. The botanical details are finely rendered, showcasing the intricate veining of the leaves and the texture of the flowers' petals.

artworks.title: Columbia Jay
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of two blue birds perched on a branch. The birds are shown in detail, with long tail feathers and crests on the tops of their heads. They are on top of a branch with green and brown leaves. The top bird holds a small nut or seed in one taloned foot and is pressing it with its beak. The background is plain off-white paper.

artworks.title: Mottled Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three owls perched on a pine branch. It features detailed illustrations of three different owls resting on the branches of a pine tree, complete with green needles and pine cones. The owl at the top left is brown with yellow eyes and intricate feather detailing. The one in the center has reddish-brown plumage with yellow eyes. The third owl at the bottom has white and brown feathers, set against the green pine branches. The composition captures the textures of the owls' feathers and the pine needles with delicate precision.

artworks.title: Marsh Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a large nest made of woven grass and twigs, with three marsh wrens perched around it. The birds have brown feathers with white and black markings. The color palette consists of natural earth tones, primarily browns and greens, accented by light touches of white. The nest is centrally positioned, one bird perches on a thin branch extending from the top left, another bird sits directly on the nest to the right, and the third wren hangs below the nest on the left.

artworks.title: Cow Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting featuring two birds on a patch of grass. Two birds are depicted in detailed naturalistic style, sitting on a small patch of ground overgrown with green moss and grass. The bird on the left has brown and gray plumage, while the bird on the right displays iridescent blue and brown feathers. They appear to be pecking or inspecting the ground. There is an array of small plants and a few clovers scattered around them. The labeling and numbering suggest this is a scientifically illustrated plate, likely used for ornithological documentation. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Green-blue or White-bellied Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two swallows in flight against a cloudy sky. The image depicts two birds engaged in an aerial maneuver. They are positioned almost in a mirrored fashion towards one another, both with wings and tails spread wide. The background is composed of soft blue hues and fluffy clouds. There is a feather floating nearby.

artworks.title: Raven
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of a raven perched on a branch with leaves and small buds. The raven is depicted in detail, including its glossy black feathers that have a slight bluish sheen. It faces the left, and its beak is slightly open, revealing its tongue. The raven is sitting on a branch, surrounded by green leaves with some mottled brown patches. Among the leaves are clusters of round, brownish buds or nuts. The background behind the bird and branch is plain beige paper.

artworks.title: Blue Jay
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of three blue jays perched on a branch. The birds have bright blue plumage with small areas of white and black, and they are depicted on a gray branch adorned with green leaves and yellow and pink flowers. The topmost bird is using its beak and foot to break open a small white egg, yolk dripping down towards a second bird below that has its wings partially extended and its beak open. The third bird on the left holds a second egg in its mouth. The background behind the birds and branch is off-white paper.

artworks.title: Canada Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched on a branch with large leaves and clusters of pink and white flowers. The color palette includes shades of green, pink, white, yellow, and dark gray. One bird is below a group of blossoms while the other bird is near a cluster of blossoms, facing right.

artworks.title: Chipping Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a Chipping Sparrow perched on a tree branch. The bird has a chestnut crown, gray face, and wings with a mix of browns and blues. The branch is adorned with leaves and white flowers. The composition is detailed and delicate, capturing both the bird and foliage realistically, in the style of John James Audubon.
